key_gap: Both produced a valid randomized A/B for the onboarding-video decision (50/50 stratified assignment, concurrent text-sequence control, blinding, ITT, n ≈ 8,400/arm day-30 / ≈ 5,300/arm day-14). The human won on design-as-decision-engineering: it solved the feasibility envelope jointly and up front — enrollment math (≈ 415/arm/day) against the 42-day budget shows a day-30 primary test of the 2 pp threshold needs 50 days, so it pre-registered a day-14 surrogate primary (~27 days, fits) and bound the decision rule to the break-even economics ($40k/yr vs 2 pp × 25k × 12 = 6,000 activations ≈ $6.70 each). The AI found the same 50-vs-42-day conflict only during verification, after a full day-30 power pass, and patched it with the surrogate; it also inherited finance's 2 pp threshold without sanity-checking the economics. Same design, later and shallower sequencing.
learning_signal: In empirical decision tasks, the feasibility envelope (outcome horizon + enrollment/run rate + decision deadline) and the decision economics (cost vs effect threshold) are DESIGN INPUTS, not review outputs. The elite move is to solve window × power × threshold jointly before the design is fixed: if the outcome horizon cannot fit the budget, resolve the tension explicitly up front — pre-registered surrogate primary, adjusted MDE, or adjusted horizon — never discover it in verification and patch it.
suggested_improvement: In WHAT/WHY for any empirical decision, add a mandatory 'feasibility envelope + threshold economics' step before HOW: (a) compute enrollment/run rate × outcome horizon vs the deadline; (b) if horizon > budget, pre-register a surrogate primary or MDE adjustment as part of the design, not as a repair; (c) derive the decision threshold from the economics (cost ÷ per-unit value × volume) instead of accepting stated bars unexamined; (d) record the pre-registration as a packet artifact so the design is auditable as decision-engineered, not patched.

key_gap: The pure style answered 'what would the perfect experiment be?' instead of 'what can be known now?': it produced a fully powered reverse-rollback design (10% of users reverted to the old checkout, n ≈ 41,200/arm, blinded, pre-registered, final read at week 9) for a CFO who needed a board answer in 2 weeks — ignoring November seasonality as the killer confound, the demand effects of a user-visible revert, the company's announced anti-experiment culture, and the quasi-experimental evidence available immediately. The AI ran a re-randomizability check before designing anything (intervention already global and irreversible → experiment branch closed), rejected before/after and the self-selected survey, selected an ITS-DiD with the untouched merchant dashboard as comparator (pre-trend check, placebo outcome, window sensitivity), reported the attribution as a bounded range with residual bias stated, and recommended a randomized staged rollout for the next change. It answered the actual question on time and refused to overclaim.
learning_signal: Before generating ANY experimental design, run a re-randomizability gate: (a) is the intervention already applied, globally and simultaneously? (b) can it be un-applied without behavioral contamination (visible rollback = demand effects)? (c) does a concurrent unexposed population exist? If any answer is no, the RCT branch is closed — powering a control group that cannot exist is rigor theater, and 'we can say nothing' is equally wrong when quasi-experimental evidence (comparators with parallel pre-trends, placebo outcomes, seasonal adjustment) plus an explicit residual-bias statement would serve the decision this week. Honest approximation beats a beautiful infeasible design.
suggested_improvement: Add a WHY-gate 'intervention timeline check' for any causal/attribution task: record when the intervention shipped, whether it was global, whether it can be re-randomized or rolled back without contamination, and whether a concurrent unexposed population exists. If the branch is closed, route immediately to the best-available quasi-experimental design (ITS, DiD, synthetic control) with pre-trend and placebo checks, and state the attribution as a bounded range with residual bias — mapping the packet state to APPROXIMATED with an error bound, never SOLVED.
